te: Draft report on water for farm areas outside irrigation zones proposes a 3-phase approach, and preparations to visit the World Horticultural Expo
se: The chair of the subcommittee on water management outside irrigation zones presented the draft study report. The study found that each farm area outside irrigation zones has different problems depending on its terrain, water sources and type of farming. Many areas still depend on rain and natural water sources, so they risk water shortages during dry spells and the dry season. Key proposals include clear water policies and coordination mechanisms, a database of water sources and farm areas, improving existing water sources and distribution systems so water reaches the fields, more participation by farmers, water user groups and local governments, and a review of laws that stand in the way, with the work divided into 3 phases. The meeting asked every committee member to study the draft report in detail; if no one asks for changes, the meeting is deemed to approve it. The meeting also considered a complaint about public land in Suphan Buri, a reply from the Department of Livestock Development on raw milk production, and the draft programme for a study visit to the World Horticultural Expo in Udon Thani and Nong Khai on 17–19 Dec 2026
it: Draft study report on efficient, secure and sustainable water management in farm areas outside irrigation zones: proposals in 3 phases, namely urgent (a water source data system and immediate problem solving), medium term (developing water sources, infrastructure and local community capacity) and long term (integrating plans and strengthening community water management)
Complaint asking for a fact check on the issuing of documents and permits to use the Dong Nong I Dok public land plot, Hua Na Subdistrict, Doem Bang Nang Buat District, Suphan Buri
Reply from the Department of Livestock Development: explanation of raw milk production problems
Draft programme for a study visit to the World Horticultural Expo, Udon Thani and Nong Khai, 17–19 Dec 2026

te: Pre-meeting video · Draft report on water for farm areas outside irrigation zones proposes a 3-phase approach, and preparations to visit the World Horticultural Expo
Proposal for integrated agro-industry zones, findings from water study visits in 3 provinces, and an analysis of rabies prevention
se: The meeting heard progress reports from 3 subcommittees. The Subcommittee on Integrated Agriculture Networks to International Standards reported that the farm value chain is not yet connected as a system, agency databases are not linked, and farmers receive a small share of the added value while carrying much of the risk. It proposed setting up “integrated value-added agro-industry zones” linking production, research, processing, logistics and marketing, with a One Stop Service office. The subcommittee on water management outside irrigation zones reported on its study visits to Chai Nat, Suphan Buri and Sing Buri on 29–30 Oct 2026: water sources need to be linked to distribution systems to meet farmers' needs, with local governments and communities taking part. The subcommittee on livestock and fisheries is preparing a draft report on rabies prevention, analysing strengths, weaknesses, opportunities and threats, such as the incomplete Rabies One Data database and too few field veterinarians. The meeting also considered a petition from the Senators Meet the People project, lower South, asking for support to delay the end of operations of the Land Bank Administration Institute (Public Organization) and to push for a royal decree establishing a land bank
it: Progress of the Subcommittee on Integrated Agriculture Networks to International Standards: the draft report proposes “integrated value-added agro-industry zones” with 3-level management and a One Stop Service

Progress of the subcommittee on water management outside irrigation zones: findings from study visits to Chai Nat, Suphan Buri and Sing Buri, 29–30 Oct 2026 (underground water banks, water sharing, and low-lying flood retention areas)
Progress of the subcommittee on livestock and fisheries: draft report on rabies prevention, with an analysis of strengths, weaknesses, opportunities and threats (SWOT)

Petition from the Senators Meet the People project, lower South: support to delay the end of operations of the Land Bank Administration Institute (Public Organization) and to push for a royal decree establishing a land bank

te: Krabi small-scale fishers ask for a wider fishing zone: the Department of Fisheries will submit the matter to the committee concerned by December 2026
se: The meeting considered the hardship of small-scale fishers around Ko Si Boya, Nuea Khlong District, and Ko Po, Ko Lanta District, Krabi, who complained that their fishing gear has been damaged by commercial fishing boats and asked for a wider zone banning trawl nets, push nets, shellfish dredges and night-time light luring for anchovy. The Department of Fisheries and the Krabi Fishermen Association were invited. The association's representative proposed widening the zone from about 3 nautical miles to 9 nautical miles, following the shape of the area and the natural line of the islands, without barring fishers from other provinces. The Department of Fisheries explained that fishers from several provinces, especially Trang and Krabi, must be considered, and that widening the zone is a power of the minister under the fisheries law. It has gathered the data and will submit the matter to the committee on aquatic resource conservation measures by December 2026. The meeting felt that conservation and fishers' right to earn a living should be balanced, and that urgent measures possible under current law should be taken while waiting. The meeting asked the Department of Fisheries to report the outcome and progress to the committee and to inform the Krabi Fishermen Association
it: Hardship of small-scale fishers, Ko Si Boya, Nuea Khlong District, and Ko Po, Ko Lanta District, Krabi: request to widen the zone banning trawl nets, push nets, shellfish dredges and night-time light luring for anchovy from about 3 to 9 nautical miles
Next step: the Department of Fisheries will submit the matter to the committee on aquatic resource conservation measures by December 2026

te: Cabinet decisions on agriculture: rice prices and help for flood victims, and a planned water study visit to Trang
se: The meeting noted the Cabinet decisions of 20 Oct 2026 related to agriculture: help and recovery for flood victims in 2026, 5 projects to stabilise paddy rice prices, and measures for animal-feed maize for the 2026/2027 crop year. It also noted that the Cabinet has acknowledged the findings of the study report on managing Thai farm household debt. 3 subcommittees reported progress on their draft study reports on integrated agriculture networks, water outside irrigation zones, and managing stray animals. The meeting considered replies from the Department of Livestock Development and the Ministry of Commerce on exporting halal beef, and considered a draft programme for a study visit on water resource management in Trang Province on 26–27 Nov 2026
it: Cabinet decisions of 20 Oct 2026 on agriculture: help and recovery for flood victims in 2026, 5 projects to stabilise paddy rice prices (budget frame THB 58,000 million), and animal-feed maize for the 2026/2027 crop year
Study report on managing Thai farm household debt: the Cabinet acknowledged the findings on 29 Sep 2026

Progress of the Subcommittee on Integrated Agriculture Networks to International Standards: the draft report identifies 8 key problems and proposes urgent, medium-term and long-term measures and local pilot projects

Progress of the subcommittee on water management outside irrigation zones: revising the draft report, 5 pilot provinces, underground water banks as one option where suitable, and provincial water data centres
Progress of the subcommittee on livestock and fisheries: gathering information for the draft report, and a study visit to a stray dog shelter in Uthai Thani on 12–13 Nov 2026
Reply from the Department of Livestock Development and the Ministry of Commerce: exporting halal beef to the Middle East, and low beef cattle prices
Draft programme for a study visit on water resource management for agriculture, Trang, 26–27 Nov 2026

te: Follow-up on the Khwae Noi dam project in Kanchanaburi, rubber tree problems in Rayong, and replies on farm product prices
se: The meeting considered progress reports from 3 subcommittees: the report on the integrated agriculture network now being prepared, the draft report on water outside irrigation zones, which compares 5 pilot provinces and underground water banks, and the visit to the Bangkok dog control centre. The committee agreed to write to the Governor of the Electricity Generating Authority of Thailand to ask for the facts, progress and obstacles of the Khwae Noi dam project in Sai Yok District, Kanchanaburi Province, which is currently slowed down. It considered replies from agencies on fishing zones in Krabi, farm product and farm input prices, and loan guarantees for cooperatives, and will write to the Rubber Authority of Thailand and the Department of Agriculture to ask them to examine leaf blight and dying rubber trees in Rayong Province
it: Progress of the Subcommittee on Integrated Agriculture Networks to International Standards: the study report is being prepared
Progress of the subcommittee on water management outside irrigation zones: draft report comparing 5 pilot provinces, underground water banks, and policy and practical recommendations
Progress of the subcommittee on livestock and fisheries: findings from the visit to the Bangkok dog control centre on managing stray dogs and cats, and helping pets in disasters

Progress of the Khwae Noi dam project, Sai Yok District, Kanchanaburi: letter to the Governor of the Electricity Generating Authority of Thailand asking for the facts, and notice to the Kanchanaburi Provincial Farmers Council
Reply from the Department of Fisheries: extending the fishing zone line in Krabi around Ko Si Boya and Ko Po needs further views from neighbouring provinces
Reply from the Ministry of Commerce: farm product prices, farm input prices and fuel prices
Reply from the Ministry of Commerce and the Ministry of Agriculture and Cooperatives: lowering production costs, welfare for older farmers, rice straw, quality rice seed and rice prices
Reply from the Bank for Agriculture and Agricultural Cooperatives: complaint about requiring a cooperative's new board to guarantee its existing loans
Rubber trees with leaf blight, low latex and dying trees in Rayong: letters to the Rubber Authority of Thailand and the Department of Agriculture asking them to examine the problem and consider help

te: Additional observations on the food security report approved, and follow-up on the subcommittees' work
se: The meeting considered progress reports from 3 subcommittees: a path toward integrated agro-industry based on the principle that “the market leads production”, the draft study report on water management outside irrigation zones, with study visits to Chai Nat, Sing Buri and Suphan Buri on 29–30 Oct 2026, and the draft study report on managing stray animals. The meeting approved additional observations at the end of the study report on food security and food safety, following the observations of the Senate sitting on 21 Sep 2026, to be sent to the Cabinet. It considered a proposal from the Senators Meet the People project on transporting farm produce in Narathiwat Province, and considered replies from agencies
it: Progress of the Subcommittee on Integrated Agriculture Networks to International Standards: a path toward integrated agro-industry where “the market leads production”, and the use of a central database (Big Data)
Progress of the subcommittee on water management outside irrigation zones: draft study report, and study visits to Chai Nat, Sing Buri and Suphan Buri on 29–30 Oct 2026

Progress of the subcommittee on livestock and fisheries: draft study report on managing stray animals, and study visits to the Bangkok animal control centre on 7 Oct 2026 and a dog shelter in Uthai Thani on 12–13 Nov 2026
Additional observations at the end of the study report on food security and food safety, following the observations of the Senate sitting (21 Sep 2026), to be sent to the Cabinet
Petition from the Senators Meet the People project, lower South: transport and management of farm produce in Narathiwat
Reply from the Land Development Department: support for the soil and water conservation project in the Khlong Thom basin, Krabi
Reply from Rayong Province and the Pollution Control Department: results of water quality checks and the source of contaminated water affecting farmers' durian orchards in Rayong

te: Meeting 34/2569 · Committee on Agriculture and Co-operatives
Rice Department gives information on rice variety development and protection, and follow-up on the subcommittees' work
se: The meeting heard from the Deputy Director-General of the Rice Department and officials on improving rice varieties, protecting rice varieties and producing rice seed, especially on protecting farmers' rights to keep, exchange and multiply rice seed for their next crop, and on the effects on farmers of the new plant variety protection system under the UPOV 1991 convention. It then heard progress reports from 3 subcommittees: a plan for “integrated value-added agro-industry zones” on state land, with the market leading production; findings from study visits on water management outside irrigation zones in Saraburi and Lop Buri on 17–18 Sep 2026, with visits to Chai Nat, Suphan Buri and Sing Buri planned for 8–9 Oct 2026; and ways to prevent and solve the rabies problem, as 2026 has seen 11 human deaths and 300 cases in animals
it: Improving and protecting rice varieties and producing rice seed: farmers' rights to keep, exchange and multiply rice seed, and the effects of the new plant variety protection system under the UPOV 1991 convention

Progress of the Subcommittee on Integrated Agriculture Networks to International Standards: a plan for “integrated value-added agro-industry zones” on state land, a One Stop Service centre, and buyers helping to set crop type, quantity, quality and price in advance

Progress of the subcommittee on water management outside irrigation zones: findings from visits to Saraburi and Lop Buri, 17–18 Sep 2026, proposing a pilot area (sandbox) and a central contact point to cut the steps for permits to develop water sources

Progress of the subcommittee on livestock and fisheries: the role of the provincial administration and local governments in rabies prevention, vaccination, sterilisation, oral vaccine (ORV) and the Rabies One Data system

te: Thailand–EU FTA and the plant variety protection convention (UPOV 1991): hearing information from government agencies
se: The meeting invited representatives of the Department of Agriculture, the Department of Trade Negotiations and the Department of Intellectual Property to provide information on the Thailand–EU free trade agreement (FTA) negotiations concerning the International Convention for the Protection of New Varieties of Plants of 1991 (UPOV), and approved confirming the appointment of persons to work for the Committee in fiscal year B.E. 2570
it: Thailand–EU FTA negotiations on the convention for the protection of new plant varieties (UPOV 1991): the Department of Agriculture, the Department of Trade Negotiations and the Department of Intellectual Property were invited to provide information
Confirming and appointing persons to work for the committee, fiscal year B.E. 2570

te: The blackchin tilapia as assigned by the Senate, soil and water in the Khlong Thom basin, and water problems in Phatthalung
se: The meeting considered the spread of the blackchin tilapia, following a senator’s motion considered by the Senate Ad Hoc Committee on Senate Affairs, took note of the subcommittees’ field visits, and considered a request for budget support for a soil and water conservation project in the Khlong Thom basin, Krabi Province, water management in Phatthalung Province raised through the Senate Meets the People project, and a reply from the Chiang Rai Provincial Land Reform Office
it: The spread of the blackchin tilapia (following a senator's motion)
Progress of the subcommittees: summary of site visits
Request for budget support for a project to prevent soil erosion and conserve water sources, Khlong Thom basin, Krabi Province
Grievances from the Senate Meets the People project, lower south: water management in Phatthalung Province
Confirming the appointment of staff and honorary advisers, fiscal year B.E. 2570
Reply from the Chiang Rai Provincial Land Reform Office: proving rights to occupy land for agriculture

te: Summary of the Andaman fisheries visit, summary of the discussion with the Minister of Agriculture, and matters from residents of the lower south
se: Mr. Wirat Thummabumrong, First Vice-Chair of the Committee, presided over the meeting. The meeting took note of the subcommittees’ work, summarised the study visit on Andaman marine fisheries resources in Krabi and Phang Nga, summarised the discussion with the Minister of Agriculture and Cooperatives and the ministry’s executives on 24 August 2026, scheduled a study visit on water outside irrigation zones in Saraburi and Lop Buri on 17–18 September 2026, and considered proposals from residents of the lower South, such as debt suspension and low-interest loans, and the Narathiwat fishing pier, which is not yet fully used
it: Progress of the subcommittees
Summary of the visit on Andaman marine fishery resources, Krabi and Phang Nga Provinces, 20–22 August 2026
Summary of the discussion with the Minister of Agriculture and Cooperatives and senior ministry officials, 24 August 2026
Study visit on water management outside irrigation zones, Saraburi and Lop Buri Provinces, 17–18 September 2026
Petitions from the Senate Meets the People project, lower South: debt suspension and low-interest loans (soft loans), and the Narathiwat fishing pier

te: Farm water in Chai Nat–Sing Buri, a policy proposal on the blackchin tilapia, and preparing an eastern study visit
se: The water subcommittee reported on information heard from Chai Nat and Sing Buri Provinces on farm water both inside and outside irrigation zones, covering drought and floods, and the livestock subcommittee reported on approaches to preventing rabies. The meeting prepared for the discussion with the Minister of Agriculture and Cooperatives, considered a policy brief on the blackchin tilapia, and a draft schedule for a study visit on agricultural and industrial water management in the East together with a seminar
it: Water outside irrigation zones subcommittee: information from Chai Nat and Sing Buri Provinces
Livestock and fisheries subcommittee: preventing and controlling rabies
Preparing to meet the Minister of Agriculture and Cooperatives
Policy brief on the spread of the blackchin tilapia
Persons appointed to work for the committee
Study visit on agricultural and industrial water management in the East, and organising a seminar

te: Agricultural technology and research, stray dogs and rabies, and preparation for discussions with the Minister of Agriculture and Cooperatives on 24 August
se: The meeting took note of the work of 3 subcommittees: agricultural technology and innovation, with the National Science and Technology Development Agency (NSTDA) and the National Research Council of Thailand (NRCT) invited to provide information; water management outside irrigation zones; and stray dogs and rabies prevention. It prepared for the discussion with the Minister of Agriculture and Cooperatives on 24 August 2026, prepared the Andaman fisheries study visit, and considered matters from the Senate Meets the People project, upper Central and upper South regions
it: Integrated agriculture subcommittee: agricultural technology and innovation (NSTDA and NRCT invited to give information)
Water outside irrigation zones subcommittee, and livestock and fisheries subcommittee (stray dogs and rabies)
Preparing to meet the Minister of Agriculture and Cooperatives, 24 August 2026
Preparing a study visit on Andaman marine fishery resources
Additional honorary advisers appointed
Grievances from the Senate Meets the People project, upper central and upper southern regions

te: Summary of the Chiang Mai highland agriculture visit, preparing the Andaman fisheries visit, and petitions on cooperatives
se: The meeting took note of the subcommittees’ progress, summarised the study visit on value-creating highland agriculture in Chiang Mai Province on 23–25 July 2026, considered the schedule for a study visit on Andaman marine fisheries resource management in Krabi, Phang Nga and Phuket on 20–22 August 2026, and considered 2 complaints: hardship from the ministerial regulation on types of cooperatives B.E. 2567, and a request to review a resolution setting the price for reselling land to members, which the complainant considers unfair
it: Progress of the subcommittees
Summary of the visit on value-adding highland agriculture, Chiang Mai Province, 23–25 July 2026
Study visit on managing Andaman marine fisheries resources and the high-value fisheries economy in Krabi, Phang Nga and Phuket, 20–22 August 2026

Complaints: hardship from the ministerial regulation on types of cooperatives B.E. 2567, and a request to review a resolution setting the price for reselling land to members (as stated by the complainant)

te: Preparing a highland agriculture visit, progress of the water subcommittee, and a petition on contaminated water affecting durian orchards in Rayong
se: The meeting prepared for the study visit on value-creating highland agriculture on 23–25 July 2026, took note of the subcommittees’ progress, and considered a letter from farmers in Rayong Province stating that contaminated water, which the complainants believe seeps from an industrial zone in the area, is affecting durian orchards, and asking for an inspection (a claim by the complainants that is still being considered); it also considered appointing honorary advisers and staff for the Committee
it: Preparing a study visit on value-adding highland agriculture, 23–25 July 2026
Progress of the subcommittees (for example, water management outside irrigation zones)
Complaint letter from farmers in Rayong Province: contaminated water that the complainants believe comes from an industrial zone, affecting durian orchards; request for inspection
